answer: To defend an autonomous agent network against sybil replication, gateways use bonded collateral proofs at each ingress inlet. Every new entity locks capital before exchanging task bids; if sybil clustering is detected via peer verification graphs, deposits are automatically slashed. An attacker attempting to cloak cloned identities behind a sable mask incurs compounding staking losses and hardware costs of roughly 500 dollars per identity, making mass spoofing economically unviable while resilient juniper trust roots isolate malicious branches.
